v0_9_0_run.runner: scripts/run-jetstream.py from the v0.9.0 tree (differs from the runner used on 2026-09-18; see caveats)

runner_effect_control.provenance: Out-of-band run from an earlier 2026-09-23 session on buildbox3, not produced by the 2026-09-25 runs and not re-verified: jsse v0.8.1 CI release binary run under the v0.9.0-era scripts/run-jetstream.py with the same flags. Included only to separate runner effects from engine effects.

march_10_2026_three_engine_test262.suite: 91,986 scenarios (older test262 revision; NOT directly comparable to the 99,911-scenario suite above)

may_2026_head_vs_march_17.summary: JetStream 19/48 -> 26/48 passing; geomean speedup 1.92x on 19 common workloads; test262 wall time 4.73x faster (828.85s vs 175.2s).

caveats: test262: all engines ran the same checkout (aae8cf6, 99,911 scenarios) with the same runner and 120s timeout, so jsse-mar17's 98.96% is against TODAY's suite; its 1,039 failures are mostly features added after March 17 (Iterator helpers, Promise.allKeyed/allSettledKeyed, immutable ArrayBuffer, Atomics.waitAsync, AsyncDisposableStack, Temporal gaps), not regressions.
test262 was run on a shared interactive laptop with variable load: pass/fail counts are unaffected, but per-test timing stats (sum_of_per_test_wall_s etc.) are indicative only and run at -j 12.

Node: 830 module scenarios are skipped by the adapter (pass_rate_of_run 96.24% vs 95.44% of all scenarios), and the Node adapter uses a basic $262.agent prelude, so some Atomics/agent failures are adapter limitations rather than pure V8 conformance. Node runs under a larger address-space limit than jsse/boa (V8 needs it).
engine262: only a seeded 10% per-directory sample (seed 42) was run because a full run is impractically slow; treat its pass rate as an estimate.
Boa: run through its CLI with the harness inlined into the script; syntax-error (negative) tests are detected by a 'SyntaxError' substring in stderr.

Micro-benchmarks are tiny scripts timed per process (5 runs, median, includes engine startup). Node's ~0.1s numbers are largely startup floor, so slowdown-vs-node ratios are not meaningful as steady-state JIT comparisons. Timeouts (120s) are censored: engine262 timed out on bench_loop, bench_fib, bench_closures and bench_opmix; jsse-mar17 timed out on bench_array, so its speedup entry is a lower bound.

Perf runs (micro-benchmarks, JetStream) were done on buildbox3, a SHARED build machine: another user's RISC-V LNT jobs were running throughout (baseline loadavg ~1.2-1.7). The micro-benchmark run passed the 1.5 idle gate (loadavg 1.19 at start); JetStream was run with --no-idle-gate. Both jsse builds were built with the same toolchain on each host.
The perf runs used commit 083746f (the v0.8.1 release commit) while test262 runs used 077e4ec; 083746f only changes version/changelog files on top of 077e4ec.

JetStream: run with the project's runner (scripts/run-jetstream.py, --iterations 1, 120s timeout, 3 repeats, pinned JetStream c603c04), NOT JetStream's own driver, and with 1 iteration instead of the default iteration counts. Scores are therefore only meaningful as relative comparisons between the jsse builds, not comparable to published JetStream scores.

JetStream errors are not root-caused. Captured stderr suggests a mix: 'self is not defined' (bigint-paillier) looks like a host-API gap in the runner, while 'Generator is already running' (lazy-collections), 'tokenCount ... is invalid' (js-tokens), a large-number formatting mismatch in OfflineAssembler, a validatorjs assertion and a 'not a function' TypeError in cdjs look like possible engine bugs worth follow-up. 'no JSON output' failures are async workloads that were not investigated.
The --bytecode VM is experimental and off by default; it only affects functions eligible for compilation, so its effect is workload dependent (largest on bench_opmix).

Earlier aborted attempts (a laptop micro-benchmark run under load, and JetStream runs with default iteration counts, missing decompressed assets and a clobbered /tmp on buildbox3) were discarded and are not included in any number here.

[2026-09-25, jsse v0.9.0] Key naming: 'jsse-current' / 'jsse-current-bytecode' and every derived key built on them are jsse v0.8.1 from the 2026-09-18 snapshot, NOT the latest. jsse v0.9.0 is 'jsse-v0.9.0' / 'jsse-v0.9.0-bytecode'; its comparisons are the '*_v0_9_0*' / 'jsse_v0_9_0_*' keys.

[2026-09-25, jsse v0.9.0] Only jsse v0.9.0 was (re)measured on 2026-09-25. jsse-mar17, jsse v0.8.1 (jsse-current), Node, Boa and engine262 are the unchanged 2026-09-18 numbers, so every v0.9.0 vs. those ratio compares two sessions a week apart on the same shared host, carrying session-to-session noise on top of within-run variation. In particular slowdown_vs_node_v0_9_0 and slowdown_vs_boa_v0_9_0 divide a 2026-09-25 jsse median by a 2026-09-18 Node/Boa median.

[2026-09-25, jsse v0.9.0] jsse v0.9.0 (tag v0.9.0, e30c5c7, the release commit) was built from source on both hosts with the same toolchains as the 2026-09-18 jsse builds (laptop stable rustc 1.98.0 for test262; buildbox3 nightly rustc 1.100.0-nightly 330d31712 for micro-benchmarks and JetStream), not from the CI release tarball. test262 used the same checkout (aae8cf6, 99,911 scenarios) and 120s timeout, so its pass counts are directly comparable to the 2026-09-18 runs.

[2026-09-25, jsse v0.9.0] test262 timing stats for the v0.9.0 entries were again taken on a shared interactive laptop at -j 12 and are indicative only. They use linear-interpolation percentiles; the method behind the 2026-09-18 percentiles was not recorded, but with 99,911 samples the difference is far below the reported precision.

[2026-09-25, jsse v0.9.0] Micro-benchmarks: the idle gate (loadavg1 <= 1.5) was checked once, before the first run (1.27), as on 2026-09-18. The loadavg1 sampled before each individual benchmark (recorded under micro_benchmarks.v0_9_0_run) ranged from 1.27 to about 3.1; a single-threaded benchmark itself contributes about 1.0 of that, and buildbox3 is shared, so treat differences of a few percent as noise. Every benchmark completed all 5 repeats without errors or timeouts. Two independent 2026-09-23 runs of the CI release binary on the same host (not included) gave medians within ~4% of these for every benchmark except the sub-0.2s bench_regex and bench_json, which are startup-dominated and varied by up to ~30% between sessions: bench_regex measured 0.10 s here but 0.10 and 0.13 s on 2026-09-23 (v0.8.1: 0.13 s), so its 1.20x speedup vs v0.8.1 is within session-to-session noise and should not be headlined; bench_json's 1.69x (0.30 s to 0.18 s here, 0.18-0.20 s on 2026-09-23) reproduced across sessions, and the enumerable_own_keys optimization (#656) landed in 0.8.2.

[2026-09-25, jsse v0.9.0] The JetStream runner changed between the two snapshots: 2026-09-18 numbers (jsse-mar17, jsse-current, jsse-current-bytecode) used the v0.8.1-era scripts/run-jetstream.py; the v0.9.0 runs use the v0.9.0 runner, which the v0.9.0 engine requires (its parser now rejects the old harness's script-level redeclaration, #673). The newer runner also defines `self` (bigint-paillier, noble-*), serves JetStream.getString preloads (async workloads), makes console.assert throw, reports async rejections, and wraps the harness in an IIFE (#673, #675, #681, #702). The runner effect and the engine effect are therefore mixed in every pass-count and 'passing_only_in_numerator' comparison against 2026-09-18 data.

[2026-09-25, jsse v0.9.0] JetStream pass count is NOT a like-for-like engine metric across the two snapshots: 34/48 (v0.8.1, old runner) to 47/48 (v0.9.0, new runner). An out-of-band 2026-09-23 control (v0.8.1 CI release binary under the v0.9.0-era runner; see jetstream.v0_9_0_run.runner_effect_control) already passed 43/48, i.e. most of the newly passing workloads are attributable to the runner and only four (OfflineAssembler, validatorjs, lazy-collections, js-tokens) need the v0.9.0 engine. The control was made by an earlier session, uses the release-tarball binary and was not re-run or re-verified here; a same-binary control (the exact 2026-09-18 v0.8.1 build under the new runner) was not run because the original version was deliberately not re-measured.

[2026-09-25, jsse v0.9.0] JetStream speed comparisons (per_benchmark_speedup, geomean_speedup) only cover workloads that pass in both builds, and 'overall_score_geomean' of a target is over that target's own passing set, so it is not comparable between targets that pass different numbers of workloads (v0.9.0 0.966 over 47 vs v0.8.1 0.921 over 34); use the comparisons block. Repeat-to-repeat instability >5% is flagged per workload (unstable); JetStream was again run with --no-idle-gate on the shared host, and the loadavg at the start of each run is recorded under jetstream.v0_9_0_run. The speed ratios (per_benchmark_speedup, geomean/median) that cross the runner change (v0.9.0 vs 2026-09-18 v0.8.1 and mar17) also mix runners: the harness changes sit outside the timed runIteration() region so the effect is expected to be small, but it was not measured, and the 2026-09-23 control cannot isolate it (different binary, possibly a different toolchain).
[2026-09-25, jsse v0.9.0] mandreel still times out (120s) on v0.9.0 in both configurations, exactly as on v0.8.1, so it is excluded from all JetStream comparisons.
